It has two switches, S1 and S2. Under normal conditions, S1 is closed and S2 is open. Under certain special conditions, S1 is open and S2 is closed. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: On the left side of the figure are HV terminals A, B, and C, and on the right side are LV terminals a, b, and c. The primary side is marked as Δ connection, and the secondary side is marked as Y connection. The LV star side has three groups of secondary windings; a is the outer end of the upper secondary winding, b is the outer end of the middle secondary winding, and c is the outer end of the lower secondary winding; the other ends of the three groups of windings are connected to the same vertical common star point/neutral connection line on the right side. In the figure, S1 is located between the C line and the lower node of the primary side, and S2 is located near the B line and can connect the B conductor to the lower Δ node. Then reason: The special condition given in the problem is S1 open, S2 closed. When S1 is open, the external C-phase power source is no longer connected to this lower node; when S2 is closed, the lower Δ node is connected to the B conductor. Tracing according to the Δ primary-side connection relation in the figure, at this time the primary windings corresponding to the a-phase winding and c-phase winding of LV are both excited by the same A-B voltage, and the effective polarity directions are the same. Therefore, the phase voltages of secondary-side a phase and c phase relative to the same star point are equal in magnitude and the same in phase. Since a and c are at the same potential relative to the common star point, the voltage difference between a and c is zero.

method.method_draft: Describe the figure first: identify the LV star connection, with terminals a and c at the outer ends of the top and bottom secondary windings and their other ends joined to the same neutral. Then impose the text condition S1 open, S2 closed. With S1 open, the external C supply is disconnected; with S2 closed, the lower delta junction is tied to the B conductor. Trace the delta primary connections and note that the primary windings corresponding to LV phases a and c are then excited by the same A-to-B voltage in the same effective sense. Therefore their secondary phase voltages relative to the common star point are equal and in phase. Since a and c sit at the same potential relative to the same neutral, the voltage magnitude across a and c is 0 V.

再推理：题设特殊条件为 S1 open、S2 closed。S1 断开时，外部 C 相电源不再接入该下部节点；S2 闭合时，下部 Δ 节点被接到 B 导体。按图中 Δ 一次侧连接关系追踪，此时与 LV 的 a 相绕组和 c 相绕组相对应的一次绕组都由同一个 A-B 电压激励，而且有效极性方向相同。因此，二次侧 a 相和 c 相相对于同一个星点的相电压大小相等、相位相同。既然 a 和 c 对公共星点处于相同电位，则 a 与 c 之间的电压差为零。

method.method_draft: Assign node symbols from the diagram: let the transformer's lower delta node be C'. From the drawn delta/Y winding correspondence, write the secondary phase voltages as proportional to the relevant primary winding voltages, e.g. V_aN = k V_AB and V_cN = k V_AC' with the polarity indicated by the winding orientation. Substitute into the transformer equations: V_cN = k V_A C' = k V_AB = V_aN. Therefore V_ac = V_aN - V_cN = 0, so the magnitude is 0 V.
